questions.prompt: Which month comes just before September?
questions.explanation: September is the first month of autumn, and the month that comes just before it is August, the last month of summer. July comes one month earlier than August, October comes just after September, and November comes later still.

questions.prompt: In which word does the throat shake on the th, as it does in the word the?
questions.explanation: Them carries the same sound as the: the tongue goes between the teeth and the throat shakes. In teeth, in three and in thanks the air simply passes and the throat stays quiet, even though all four words begin or end with the same two letters.

questions.prompt: Read: "There is no cloud in the sky and the air is hot." Complete the answer: "It's ___."
questions.explanation: After It's the weather is described with adjectives, so sun becomes sunny and hot stays as it is: It's sunny and hot. The answers built on the noun sun never describe the day, and hotter compares this day with another one, which the sentence never does.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Next spring the days ___ longer, and the nights ___ shorter."

options.text: will be ... will not to be

questions.explanation: In spring the days really do grow longer and the nights really do grow shorter, so both halves say what will happen and both take will be. The negative won't would deny one of the two facts, and will not to be adds a word that never follows will.

questions.prompt: Which description of December has no mistake?

options.text: December is more cold than March, and it is a snow month.
December is cold than March, and it is a snowy month.
December is colder than March, and it is a snowy month.
December is colder that March, and it is a snowy month.

questions.explanation: Two rules meet here: a short adjective compares with -er and than, which gives colder than March, and a month is described by the adjective built with a y, which gives a snowy month. Every other sentence breaks at least one of them: more cold and the noun snow in one, a bare cold in another, and that instead of than in the third.

questions.prompt: Which list of activities is correctly spelled?
questions.explanation: Swim is consonant plus vowel plus consonant, so its last letter doubles before -ing: swimming. Walk ends in two consonants and takes -ing as it is, and play keeps its y and gives playing; every other list forgets the doubling of swim, doubles the k of walk, or cuts a letter out of playing.
